speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To understand the root cause of your double vision, limb weakness, and difficulty climbing stairs, can you tell me if you experience any muscle twitching or fatigue that worsens with activity and improves with rest?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the fluctuation of weakness and diplopia worsening with gaze changes is very specific. Have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids or slurred speech, and do your symptoms tend to cluster in episodes throughout the day?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: That lack of fever and family history makes an acute infection or genetic neuropathy less likely, but the symmetrical, activity-induced weakness combined with gaze-dependent diplopia strongly suggests a neuromuscular junction issue. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_receptor_antibodies. REQUEST TEST: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.
